transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

It's very nice to meet you too, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing. It's probably just me being a bit overly sensitive, but... even on my better days lately, I just can't seem to shake this feeling. It's a little embarrassing to say out loud, honestly, because I don't want you to think poorly of me. But I've been feeling like some of the people at my church, and in my walking club, are... well, watching me. And sometimes it seems like they're putting little messages about me in the church bulletin, or hiding things in what they say when I'm around. 

I know that probably sounds a bit silly, and I really do try to just brush it off. Is it okay that I came in for something like that? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by talking to you about it.
Have you been feeling unusually high, excited, or full of energy lately?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I hope that's okay to say, but no, I haven't felt like that at all. 

If anything, I just feel a bit... well, quiet and tired lately. I really try not to be a complainer, so I hope it's alright to admit that. But no, definitely no extra energy or excitement. Did I answer that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Oh... um... well. I'm a little hesitant to say, just because I really don't want you to think I'm... you know, losing my mind or anything. I know how that sounds. 

But... yes, I suppose I have. Just a little bit. Sometimes when the house is very quiet, I'll hear my name being called. Or just a few words, and it sounds exactly like my friend's voice coming from the kitchen, or maybe out on the porch. It's so clear that I actually answer back out loud before I remember that nobody is there with me. 

It's probably just my imagination playing tricks on me because I'm on my own so much, right? Is it okay that I mentioned that? I really hope it doesn't make me sound too foolish.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have my moments where I feel a little blue, just like anybody else, I suppose. Especially being on my own so much. But certainly not all day, or every day. 

I really try to count my blessings and keep a smile on, you know? I'd hate to be a bother to anyone by just moping around the house. I hope that's the right answer... I just wouldn't want you to think I'm deeply depressed or not trying my best to stay positive. Does that make sense?
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Oh... well, I suppose a little bit, maybe? I really don't want to sound like I'm just giving up on things, because I do try to stay busy. I know how important that is. 

But, um... I used to just love being out in my garden, and I'd do quite a bit of quilting. I always used to read a chapter or two before bed, too. Lately, though... well, the quilt basket just sort of sits there untouched. And I'm afraid I've let the weeds take over the garden a bit... I just haven't cared quite as much to go out there and tend to it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy. I really do mean to get back to it all soon. Is it normal to just need a little break from your hobbies sometimes?
Have you had any recent medical illness or problems with your brain or nerves?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... nothing like that at all. I mean, I have the usual little aches and creaks, just from getting older, I suppose. But certainly no major medical illnesses, and definitely nothing wrong with my nerves or my brain. 

Physically, I've been very blessed, actually. I try my best to take good care of myself so I don't become a burden to anyone, you know? I really hope that's what you were asking... is it okay that I just have a clean bill of health there?
About how long have you been feeling that people are watching you or sending you messages?

Oh... um, well... I suppose it's been a little while now. I really hate to even talk about it, because I know how strange it must sound. I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind or anything like that. I really do try to keep things together.

But, um... if I'm being perfectly honest... the things on the television, and the voices, and just... having such a hard time keeping my thoughts straight... I guess it's been going on for about eleven months now. 

I've tried so hard to just ignore it and be normal, you know? I didn't want to make a fuss. I hope you don't think less of me for letting it go on this long without saying anything. Is it... is it okay that I'm finally telling you about it now?
During the past eleven months, have you had a period when you felt unusually happy or euphoric?

Oh, no, no. Goodness, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I'm just a very even-keeled person, usually. I try to stay positive, of course, because nobody likes a complainer, but... no, I haven't had any times where I was just over the moon or acting out of sorts like that. 

I really do try to just keep my head down and be pleasant. I hope that's the right answer... I just wouldn't want you to think I was prone to being overly dramatic or anything. Is it alright that I just sort of stay in the middle, most of the time?
During these eleven months, have you had a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Oh... um, well... I suppose I have been feeling a bit down. I really don't like to complain, you know, because I know everyone has their struggles, and I don't want to be a bother to anyone. I've always tried to just put on a brave face and keep going.

But, um... yes, if I'm being completely honest, it's been quite difficult. I've just felt this... this deep sadness, and I feel so guilty all the time, though I'm not entirely sure why. And things I used to enjoy just don't seem to hold any interest for me anymore. 

It's actually been going on for a little while before the other things started... I'd say about a year and two months now. I'm so sorry, I probably should have mentioned it sooner. I just didn't want to seem like a burden or like I wasn't trying hard enough to be happy. Is it... is it okay that I'm admitting this to you now? I really hope you don't think I'm just feeling sorry for myself.
Was there ever a time when the voices or messages were happening for at least two weeks while you were not feeling depressed?

Oh... well, let me think. I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I don't want to confuse things. 

Um, there actually was a little spell, maybe for a few weeks or so... where I was feeling a bit brighter. I was getting dressed every day, and eating a little better, and just... not feeling quite so weighed down by everything. I was really trying my best to pull myself together, you know? 

But... even during that nicer time, when my mood was better... I was still hearing my name being called in the empty house. And... and I still had this awful feeling that the people at church were dropping hints about me when they talked. I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible, and I really tried to just ignore it and be a good parishioner. I hope you don't think I'm making things up... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

Oh... um, well... I suppose my daughter has mentioned something like that once or twice. I really try to be clear, I do. I just want to be helpful and make sure I'm giving all the right details. 

But sometimes, when I try to explain things... like, I might start with a thought about the mail, or something that happened at church, and then... well, I just sort of end up talking about quilt patterns, or the birds outside, or... or those warnings I feel like I'm getting. And then I look at whoever I'm talking to, and I can just see on their face that they don't know what I'm getting at. 

I feel so terrible when it happens, because I don't want to confuse anyone or take up too much of their time. I just get a little tangled up, I guess. I hope that doesn't make me sound foolish... I really am trying my best to make sense. Is it okay that I get a little off track sometimes?
During that time when you were feeling brighter, did the voices and messages continue for at least one month?

Oh, um... well, I know I mentioned that little spell earlier, where I felt a bit brighter for a few weeks... I hope I didn't make it sound longer than it was. I just wanted to show that I really was trying to get better. 

But, um, yes... even during those several weeks when I was getting dressed and eating better, and feeling less weighed down... I was still hearing my name when I was alone in the house. And I still had those thoughts about the people at church hinting about me. 

So... I suppose it wasn't quite a full month that I felt better, just those few weeks. But the voices and the hints, they didn't stop during that time. I'm sorry, I hope I'm being clear enough. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way... is that what you needed to know?
At any time during these past eleven months, were the voices and the messages going on for a full month when you were not feeling depressed?

Oh, um... well, let me think about the whole eleven months. I really want to be accurate for you. I don't want to mislead you at all. 

You know, I think... well, for almost this entire stretch of time, the sadness and that heavy guilt, and just not caring about my usual hobbies... they've just been there. Like a shadow, I suppose. Even on the days when the voices were quiet, or when I didn't feel quite so worried about the church folks... the sadness was still lingering in the background. 

So, I don't think there was ever a full month where I felt completely free of the depression while the other things were happening. I really have tried to keep my chin up, though, I promise. I hope I'm not being too much of a bother with all this... does that answer what you were looking for?

But, um, yes... even during those several weeks when I was getting dressed and eating better, and feeling less weighed down... I was still hearing my name when I was alone in the house. And I still had those thoughts about the people at church hinting about me. 

So... I suppose it wasn't quite a full month that I felt better, just those few weeks. But the voices and the hints, they didn't stop during that time. I'm sorry, I hope I'm being clear enough. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way... is that what you needed to know?

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been at least a one-month period of psychotic symptoms in the absence of a major depressive episode, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia here.
doctor.question: At any time during these past eleven months, were the voices and the messages going on for a full month when you were not feeling depressed?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: For most of this whole stretch, the sadness, guilt, and loss of interest have been there in the background, even during times when the voices or suspicious thoughts were quieter.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there was any period of a full month where psychotic symptoms occurred without depression. This relates to assessing whether the depressive episode has been present for the majority of the illness's duration (Criterion C).

patient.answer:
Oh, um... well, let me think about the whole eleven months. I really want to be accurate for you. I don't want to mislead you at all. 

You know, I think... well, for almost this entire stretch of time, the sadness and that heavy guilt, and just not caring about my usual hobbies... they've just been there. Like a shadow, I suppose. Even on the days when the voices were quiet, or when I didn't feel quite so worried about the church folks... the sadness was still lingering in the background. 

So, I don't think there was ever a full month where I felt completely free of the depression while the other things were happening. I really have tried to keep my chin up, though, I promise. I hope I'm not being too much of a bother with all this... does that answer what you were looking for?

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms occur in the context of a prolonged depressive episode, and there was no full month of psychosis without depression; this rules out F20.0 and supports schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.

opening_question.intent: Understand the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms for about 11 months, including auditory hallucinations, persecutory/reference delusions, and disorganized thought/speech. She also has a sustained depressive syndrome with sadness, guilt, and anhedonia lasting about 14 months. A key schizoaffective criterion is met because psychotic symptoms persisted for at least 2 weeks during a period when mood was better, while mood episodes were present for the majority of the overall illness duration. There is no evidence of mania/hypomania, and no medical cause was identified.
